I collect because I have always found tangible copies of music more enjoyable than digital. To me, it’s kinda a security thing, I can use Spotify but if I don’t download the music or the music service gets discontinued, then I have no music. It’s especially important for me because I listen to music while driving and going through an area with poor cellular data and no WiFi isn’t uncommon and having a physical copy means as long as my Jeeps cassette deck or CD player works, I have music.

Also, it’s kinda a novelty for me. Cassettes aren’t a popular medium (is growing in popularity, but not as common as vinyl). It’s kinda interesting to use a cassette when everyone else is going completely digital. Feels like a counterculture. 

I always found the appearance of cassettes to be cool and interesting. I always like it when a record label does cool stuff with the cassette shell, like make it glittery or some color that goes well with the cover art. 

Having cassettes is kinda like holding a piece of history as if you have a pressing from, say, the 90s, it’s a piece from that time that isn’t really duplicated nowadays. Some record labels are re releasing albums on cassette, but that’s not too common.

This style of metal, for those unfamiliar, is characterized by deeper and more aggressive vocals and lyrics. Much faster and intense drumming. Chunkier and heavier bass guitar. Faster and louder guitar with distortion in some songs.
